btw pro tip for the new guys: during a bull market you should actually be doing *less*, not more

by over-rotating on your positions trying to catch the latest thing, or worst still, chase what is pumping, you mathematically erode your gains 

ex:
→ you hold $10k of token X. it doesn't move for weeks
→ you get bored, sell it, and buy token Y, which is already up 50%
→ Y goes up another 10%. you're at $11k. you feel smart. you don't take profit
→ Y cools off and drops 27% from the top. you're now at $8k
→ meanwhile X, the token you sold, finally runs 50%

if you had done nothing: $15k
because you "did something": $8k. 7k gap from one rotation, and a +25% to get back to where you started

in a bull market, the most important thing to do, is sit on your hands. ideally you should have planned, allocated, and all you have left to do now

is to hold.

This is excellent. So much of agentic work is actually classification: routing to the right path, choosing the next action, or triaging context.

Imagine an email agent with 500 new emails but room for only 20 in its context window. Before any real reasoning begins, it needs to identify messages from important people, active projects, or urgent threads.

For each email, Jev could return something directly usable by code:

include_in_context: true
category: active_project
urgency: 0.91
confidence: 0.97

Jev could be a game changer for latency and cost. Instead of generating an answer token by token, it returns typed decisions and probabilities in parallel.

And it’s much more versatile than training a traditional BERT-style classifier for every task. This is excellent. So much of agentic work is actually classification: routing to the right path, choosing the next action, or triaging context.

Imagine an email agent with 500 new emails but room for only 20 in its context window. Before any real reasoning begins, it needs to identify messages from important people, active projects, or urgent threads.

For each email, Jev could return something directly usable by code:

include_in_context: true
category: active_project
urgency: 0.91
confidence: 0.97

Jev could be a game changer for latency and cost. Instead of generating an answer token by token, it returns typed decisions and probabilities in parallel.

And it’s much more versatile than training a traditional BERT-style classifier for every task. You keep the flexibility of a prompt + runtime context, with the speed and predictable output of a classifier. Basically the programmability of a language model shaped like a classifier so it’s very cool. Congrats @CompleteSkeptic, you cooked!
